business_process: Water treatment and chemical feed (WTP-R1 and WTP-R2)
description: Run 26 wells, lime softening, reverse osmosis, chloramination, and pH adjustment to produce treated water for 171,400 people and the wholesale city
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Usable storage covers about 8 hours of average demand after fire reserve; loss of treatment or unsafe chemical feed is a public health event and a Tier 1 notice trigger; RTO is the time to run production in manual mode; RPO is the age of the last known-good PLC logic and setpoints
manual_workaround: Local (manual) control of wells, softeners, RO trains, and chemical feed by licensed operators; hardwired stroke limits and analyzer alarms stay active
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (Regional PLCs); SYS-01 (not required in manual mode); plant power
dependent_third_parties: Chemical suppliers; electric utility; fuel contractor; Integrator A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Licensed operators at WTP-R1 and WTP-R2; Plant Managers
quantified_operational_impact: 26 MGD average production; each hour without treatment draws down about 1 MG of usable storage
quantified_regulatory_impact: Failure or significant interruption in key treatment processes can require a Tier 1 notice within 24 hours (40 CFR 141.202); a residual below the state minimum for more than 4 hours must be reported by the end of the next business day (141.405(a)(1))
public_health_impact: Severe: under- or over-feed of disinfectant or caustic reaching 171,400 people
erp_1433_linkage: 300i-2(b)(2) plans and procedures; (b)(3) actions and equipment that lessen impact (manual mode, hardwired limits)

description: Run 10 wells, aeration, chlorination, and corrosion control for 63,500 people
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Storage covers about 10 hours of average demand; manual operation is drilled once a year only
manual_workaround: Local control by licensed operators; hardwired limits and alarms
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (Lakes PLCs); SYS-05 (Lakes SCADA, not required in manual mode)
dependent_third_parties: Chemical suppliers; electric utility; Integrator B
quantified_regulatory_impact: Same Tier 1 and Ground Water Rule clocks as BP-01

business_process: Water treatment and chemical feed (WTP-G1 and WTP-G2)
description: Run 7 wells and chlorination at two plants for 27,400 people; WTP-G2 is unstaffed and monitored remotely
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Storage covers about 12 hours; RTO is 2 hours because WTP-G2 is unstaffed and the on-call operator drives about 35 minutes; known-good logic exists only at Integrator B (RPO not achievable today)
manual_workaround: Local control by licensed operators; on-call operator to WTP-G2; hardwired limits and alarms
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (Ridge PLCs); SYS-05 (Ridge SCADA); SYS-04 (Integrator B agent)
dependent_third_parties: Integrator B; chemical suppliers; electric utility
quantified_operational_impact: 3.6 MGD average production; WTP-G2 unstaffed nights and weekends
quantified_regulatory_impact: Same Tier 1 and Ground Water Rule clocks as BP-01

description: Run 1-3 wells and a chlorination skid at each of 8 small systems (11,600 people)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Small storage; roving operators reach each site within 4 hours; controller logic is not backed up
manual_workaround: Roving operator runs the well and chlorinator by hand; portable chlorine test kits
quantified_regulatory_impact: Tier 1 notice if disinfection fails and water reaches customers; daily residual records (141.403(b)(3)(i)(B))
public_health_impact: Severe at site level: loss of disinfection for up to 2,900 people per system
erp_1433_linkage: Not required to certify (300i-2(e) guidance only); covered by the company ERP practice voluntarily

description: Keep system pressure with 18 booster stations and 14 storage tanks across the 3 covered systems, and tank levels at small systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Low pressure risks backflow and triggers precautionary boil water notices; boosters have local pressure-switch control
manual_workaround: Local pressure-switch control; roving operators set pumps by hand
quantified_operational_impact: 18 boosters; 14 tanks; a pressure loss in one zone affects about 8,000 to 20,000 people
quantified_regulatory_impact: Precautionary boil water notice and possible Tier 1 notice for a natural disaster or pressure loss affecting distribution (141.202(a) item (7))
public_health_impact: Severe: backflow and contamination risk during low pressure

business_process: Centralized supervisory monitoring and control (ROC and SCADA)
description: 24x7 remote monitoring, alarms, and control of all plants and 75 remote sites; read-only monitoring of Lakes and Ridge
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Manual operation and roving checks of about 100 sites can be sustained about 48 hours with overtime and WARN mutual aid; historian RPO 24 hours because operators also keep paper logs; after a cyber incident SCADA is restored only after it is verified clean
manual_workaround: Manual plant operation; 6 roving operator trucks on 4-hour site rounds; paper logs
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: Integrator A; Integrator B; radio and cellular carriers; MSSP
dependent_people_or_facilities: ROC operators; SCADA engineers; Plant Managers
quantified_operational_impact: About 100 sites (41 PLC sites, 75 RTU sites, some shared) need in-person checks every 4 hours
quantified_regulatory_impact: No direct rule on SCADA itself; missed monitoring caused by the outage is reportable within 48 hours (141.31(b)); grab sampling every 4 hours when continuous monitoring fails, restored within 14 days (141.403(b)(3)(i)(A))
public_health_impact: Moderate: slower detection of process upsets while operators run manually

business_process: Water quality monitoring, laboratory, and compliance reporting
description: Online analyzers, grab samples, the in-house certified lab, and monthly reporting to the state
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Disinfectant residual must be verified during any treatment disruption; missed compliance monitoring is a violation reportable within 48 hours (141.31(b)); continuous residual monitoring failure requires grab samples every 4 hours
manual_workaround: Grab samples every 4 hours at plant outlets and 22 distribution stations; portable kits; paper bench sheets
quantified_operational_impact: About 160 compliance and process samples a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed monitoring reportable within 48 hours; monthly results due within the first 10 days of the following month (141.31(a))
public_health_impact: Severe: an unverified residual can hide a disinfection failure

description: Activate the ERP, consult the primacy agency, and issue Tier 1, boil water, and consecutive-system notices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Tier 1 notice no later than 24 hours after learning of the situation and primacy agency consultation within 24 hours (141.202(b)); the wholesale city must also be notified (141.201(c)(1)); RTO 4 hours leaves time to decide and draft inside the 24 hours even if the CIS and email are down
manual_workaround: Offline contact exports; broadcast media; posting and door hangers; printed templates in English and Spanish
dependent_third_parties: Broadcast media; primacy agency; printer; mass notification vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Emergency Management and Resilience Manager; Water Quality and Compliance Manager; Communications Manager
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 273,900 people and the wholesale city to reach within 24 hours
quantified_regulatory_impact: Tier 1 timing and content (141.202, 141.205); certification within 10 days (141.31(d))
public_health_impact: Severe: people keep drinking unsafe water if notice is late

business_process: Remote monitoring and after-hours alarm response for municipal clients
description: Monitor the 3 clients' plants from the ROC after hours, acknowledge alarms within 15 minutes, and call out client on-call staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract requires alarm acknowledgment within 15 minutes; after 4 hours clients must staff their own plants overnight; alarm history RPO 1 hour supports client compliance records
manual_workaround: Clients' own auto-dialers call their on-call staff directly; ROC phones clients by printed list
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (ROC); SYS-04 (client VPN read-only links); SYS-15
quantified_regulatory_impact: Client SDWA duties stay with the clients; the company owes contract notice within 24 hours of an incident affecting client monitoring
public_health_impact: Severe for client systems if alarms go unanswered
erp_1433_linkage: Not the company's 1433 duty; supports the clients' own ERPs by contract

description: Answer calls on outages, notices, water quality, and service orders for own and client customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Call volume rises 5 to 10 times during notices; account lookup depends on the CIS
manual_workaround: Scripted answers; paper service order forms; IVR outage message; callbacks after restoration
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,800 calls a day normally; 15,000 or more during a notice
quantified_regulatory_impact: Notice content must be available to callers (141.205)

description: Bill 107,800 accounts in monthly cycles and take payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $7.3 million billed per month; a 5-day delay defers about $1.2 million of cash rather than losing it; tariff rules allow estimated bills
manual_workaround: Delay the cycle; estimated bills; the processor keeps taking payments
dependent_third_parties: CIS vendor; payment processor; bank; print and mail vendor
quantified_operational_impact: 20 billing cycles a month; about 5,400 bills a business day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Tariff billing rules set by the state utility regulator

description: Bill 15,600 client accounts under each client's name and remit collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract requires cycles within 2 business days of schedule; late cycles carry service credits and damage the SOC 2 relationship
manual_workaround: Delay with client approval; estimated bills
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,300 bills a business day for clients
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contract service levels; client remittance timing

description: Collect reads for billing and leak alerts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Meters store interval data for several days; 26,800 meters are read manually anyway

business_process: Field operations, main breaks, and work orders
description: Main breaks, valves, hydrants, locates, flushing, and work orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Crews need maps and valve locations quickly to isolate breaks and limit pressure loss
manual_workaround: Printed map books in each truck; radio dispatch
quantified_operational_impact: About 40 work orders a day; 2 to 3 main breaks a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Locate requests under state one-call rules (timing outside this analysis)

description: Order, receive, and track treatment chemicals at all plants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plants hold 5 to 14 days of chemicals; orders need the finance suite and supplier portals
manual_workaround: Phone orders to suppliers; paper receiving logs
public_health_impact: Moderate if stocks run low during an extended outage

description: Time capture, payroll, onboarding and termination, and month-end close
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; missed payroll has legal and retention impact, especially during emergency overtime
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the payroll provider

business_process: Engineering, capital planning, and asset management
description: Capital projects, GIS edits, asset condition, and main replacement planning (AI-005)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Planning work can be deferred for weeks

business_process: Water quality analytics and AI decision support
description: Advisory anomaly alerts (AI-001) and the chemical dose recommender pilot (AI-002)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Advisory only; SCADA alarms and grab sampling are the controls of record
manual_workaround: None needed; operators rely on SCADA alarms and sampling
